The Agenda-Looping Assembler (fictional)
Fictional patent sketch.

FIGURE 1
```text
[A: perpetual motion whiteboard — displays meeting topics]
                   ↓
[B: consensus-seeking gavel — bangs when agreement is reached]
                   ↓
[C: action-item deferral chute — sends tasks to next meeting]
```

CLAIM 1 — An apparatus for generating an endless cycle of discussion about the cessation of discussion, ensuring that the primary output remains the discussion itself.

BENCH TEST — In this imagined conference room, the whiteboard displays "Streamlining Communication." The gavel bangs, signifying agreement to form a subcommittee. The chute accepts the subcommittee's charter and sends it to the next meeting's agenda. The whiteboard then displays "Review Subcommittee Charter."

PULL A PART
A displays topics; B signals agreement; C defers tasks. Choose which function to interrupt.

Question outside the patent: what if the meeting's purpose was explicitly to *not* decide anything?
